name: LampLinc
description: The SwitchLinc, LampLinc and ApplianceLinc code base as used by the LampLinc, the other plug-in and socket dimmers, and the older In-LineLinc dimmers.

operatingFlags.name: programmingLock
operatingFlags.description: Linking and programming from the device itself are locked out.

operatingFlags.name: ledOnTransmit
operatingFlags.description: The status LED blinks when the device sends an Insteon message.

operatingFlags.name: resumeDim
operatingFlags.description: Turning the load on at the device restores its last level instead of the on-level.

verification.note: The Insteon Developer's Guide reads bit 4 of the 0x00 reply as LED on, but later sources read it as LED off, the state 0x08 sets.

operatingFlags.name: loadSense
operatingFlags.description: Load sense is on: the device turns its load on when it senses the attached lamp or appliance being switched on.

operatingFlags.name: cleanupReport
operatingFlags.description: The device sends a success report after the cleanup messages that follow a group command. Only dealer firmware has this setting.

readings.name: databaseDelta
readings.description: A count that goes up whenever the ALL-Link database changes.

values.name: ledDimming
values.description: How much the status LED is dimmed: 0x00 is no dimming (brightest), 0x01 the most dimming and 0xFF the least.

values.name: x10HouseCode
values.description: The X10 house code, or 0x20 for no X10 address.

values.name: rampRate
values.description: The ramp rate, from 0x01 (8 minutes) to 0x1F (0.1 second). 0x00 is 2 seconds.

values.name: onLevel
values.description: The level the load turns on to, from 0x00 (off) to 0xFF (full).

values.name: signalToNoiseLastFailure
values.description: The signal-to-noise value of the last failure.

notes: The Insteon Developer's Guide lists 0x0A and above as unused on this code base; later sources add the cleanup report commands 0x0A and 0x0B.
Earlier sources give ramp rates 0x00 through 0x1F as 9 minutes down to 0.1 second; the later ones make 0x01 8 minutes and 0x00 2 seconds.
Earlier sources give D12 as the signal-to-noise ratio and D13 as a count of messages with CRC errors.
